findings.summary: Catalog curation leaked operational/back-end collections and product_type values as customer queries on larger stores (Allbirds tier/msrp, Brooklinen allow-discounts/content, Gymshark taxonomy-path product_types), cascading into false report issues and a coverage regression.

Bombas is Shopify but returns 404 on /products.json, /collections.json, and /suggest.json (public JSON endpoints disabled), so platform detection fell to unknown and catalog discovery/curation were unavailable. The Shopify adapter assumes public JSON endpoints on the primary domain.

Curated queries can regress coverage versus the starter run (Allbirds 90%->70%) when curated queries perform worse; the app has no guard to prevent a worse curated pack from lowering a store's standing.

Report emits customer-facing search/autocomplete issues for curated queries without weighting query confidence; garbage queries produced false zero-result and no-suggestion findings. Largely mitigated by FND-GEN017-001 but a query-confidence signal would harden it.

DS3 attribute observation is apparel-lexicon-biased; home-goods (Brooklinen) and beauty (ColourPop) product titles yielded zero attribute rows. Facet-markup-derived attributes would generalize DS3 across verticals.

Pipeline robustness confirmed: across five real stores in five verticals, every cycle stage either succeeded or degraded honestly with no crashes; the one aborted stage (Bombas curation) failed with a clear, correct reason.

Cached site profiles were reused by age only, so a profile captured before a discovery-schema change (pre-GEN-018, missing catalog_discovery.collections) silently degraded browse inventory to FAIL on Dress Up though the store was fine.
findings.status: fixed_gen019_schema_version_gate_on_cache_reuse (bumped site-profile to v0.2; reuse now requires matching schema)

findings.summary: The Storage / data-management (cleanup) panel exists in the sidebar but is buried below the inspection list, so the operator could not find it; it should be a discoverable settings location and cover screenshot/capture cleanup explicitly.
Inspection runs are spawned independently with no concurrency control, risking rate-limit (429) collisions and hiding what is in flight.
The dataset viewer was a navigation dead end with no way back to the originating inspection.
Cleanup removed run directories but left inspection-history rows, so the inspection list showed deleted runs as phantom entries (46 rows, 6 real runs).
Identified Shopify sites (target manifests) persist through cleanup but have no UI list, so cleaning all runs makes the sites disappear from view; sites should be first-class and re-inspectable.
Operator directive: the assistant must not trigger inspection runs; only the operator runs inspections via the UI. Validation must use existing runs on disk and never spawn a run.
The dashboard shows a flat list of runs and reports; it should present the real hierarchy (Site > Run > Results) with the connection always visible so every result traces to its inspection and site.

findings.title: Home Depot is out of scope: custom enterprise stack + Akamai bot wall + robots disallow
findings.summary: Operator requested a full evaluation of homedepot.com. Detected: custom enterprise platform (THD) behind Akamai (not Shopify/WooCommerce; products.json + wp-json both 404). Every automated request returns 403 Access Denied from Akamai Bot Manager (_bman/akavpau cookies) even with a browser UA. robots.txt explicitly disallows the discovery surfaces we inspect (/*Search?*, /*Ntt-*, /*Ntk-*, /*AjaxNavigation*). A full evaluation would require bypassing bot protection and ignoring robots.txt on disallowed paths — declined. No run performed, no bypass attempted. Legitimate path would be an authorized API / partner access or a consented manual evaluation.

findings.title: Inconsistent term->node mapping: the same product returns wildly different results by term (category vs synonym)
findings.summary: Tested 28 equivalent term pairs; 17 show materially different result sets (>=40% divergence or wrong products). Bidirectional: synonyms collapse (sheetrock 33/drywall 2411; liquid nails 17/construction adhesive 1605; roundup 249/weed killer 3078; zip ties 267/cable ties 1602; dremel 1508/rotary tool 5616) AND generic category terms fail (concrete mix 20 wrong/quikrete 643; locking pliers 106/vise grips 1161; utility knife 207/box cutter 525; oriented strand board 173/osb 378). ~11 pairs map well (plexiglass=acrylic, teflon=plumbers tape, sawzall~=reciprocating saw). Full set in assessments/homedepot/search-eval/category-synonym-pairs.json.

findings.title: Industry West legacy search has no natural-language intent handling (9/9 intent queries return zero)
findings.summary: All 9 job-function/intent queries return 0 products on industrywest.com native WooCommerce search: furnish a living room, bar stools for a kitchen island, home office, dining set for 6, small space seating, entryway furniture, reading chair, restaurant chairs, outdoor seating. Overall 32/50 (64%) of the furniture query pack is zero-result. Each replayable at https://www.industrywest.com/wp-json/wc/store/v1/products?search=<term> (X-WP-Total header). Evidence: assessments/industrywest/search-eval/SE-20260713/iw-captures.json. Customer impact: shoppers using natural phrasing hit dead-ends on products the store stocks. Business impact: lost conversions on intent traffic. Recommendation: add synonym/intent layer or a search app. Supersedes the weakly-grounded WOO-20260730 "intent 0/4" claim (which searched promo category labels like "Under $500"). [CORRECTED 2026-08-08: superseded by CORR-SR-001 — original capture measured the wrong search engine (Woo Store API / loose Shopify query) instead of the real shopper storefront; re-captured and re-graded. Net story changed.]

findings.title: Seven Bonde new search trades precision for recall (39% of results not relevant)
findings.summary: Seven Bonde (new Shopify storefront, Storefront GraphQL products(query:)) mean grade 1.78 vs IW 2.69; 39% of 145 returned items graded <=2->actually <=1 (not relevant). Head-to-head on the 15 queries BOTH answer: IW 2.67 vs SB 1.99. Noise examples (replayable via site search box): coffee table->Hemlock Ottoman; sofa->lounge chairs/benches/ottomans; dining table->Circuit Bar Stool + Heath Raster Lamp; black metal stool->EEX side tables. NDCG (0.936) FLATTERS SB because the judge grades cross-category junk 1 not 0 (validated bias is conservative). Evidence: assessments/industrywest/search-eval/SE-20260713/sb-captures.json, sb-ndcg-results.json, gold-labels.json. Recommendation: relevance thresholding to suppress low-grade results. [rubric-pinned 2026-08-06: re-run under Cortex rubric 99a0e992a992 confirms the finding - SB not-relevant 41% (mean grade 1.77) vs IW 0% (2.73); aggregate NDCG stable IW 0.944->0.953, SB 0.936->0.935.] [CORRECTED 2026-08-08: superseded by CORR-SR-001 — original capture measured the wrong search engine (Woo Store API / loose Shopify query) instead of the real shopper storefront; re-captured and re-graded. Net story changed.]

findings.title: CONTEXT: Industry West is replatforming to Seven Bonde (Shopify); evaluation covers both live storefronts
findings.summary: industrywest.com/collections/* issues 301 redirects to sevenbonde.com (verified: /collections/seating->sevenbonde.com, http 200). Seven Bonde is a live Shopify store (2390 shopify refs) re-hosting IW catalog (product image files named industry_west_product_*) plus net-new SKUs (e.g. Aero Stackable, Burton Leather Dining Chair not in IW 246-SKU catalog). Both storefronts are live; "Shop All" already routes shoppers to Seven Bonde. Not a defect; sets the evaluation target (old vs new). Evidence: assessments/industrywest/search-eval/SE-20260713/ (captures), inspection notes.

findings.title: Reproducibility gap closed: SE-20260713 NDCG was not rubric-pinned; determinism verified and baseline re-pinned
findings.summary: Replaying a query surfaced that the original SE-20260713 NDCG values were computed under an earlier Cortex default rubric and the poll script did not record rubric_hash, so exact NDCG did not reproduce against the evolved rubric (e.g. bench 0.803 vs a transient 1.000). Root-caused: the JUDGE IS DETERMINISTIC at a fixed rubric (verified: bench 3/3, armchair 4/4, restaurant chairs 4/4, probe 5/5 identical). Re-ran BOTH sets under pinned rubric 99a0e992a992: 38/49 queries reproduce exactly, 10 shifted with rubric evolution, aggregate stable within +-0.01. Fix: results now carry rubric_hash; eval-board.json holds per-query old+pinned NDCG + replay pointers (search_call + Cortex job). Evidence: assessments/industrywest/search-eval/SE-20260713/eval-board.json, iw-ndcg-rerun.json, sb-ndcg-rerun.json. Recommendation: always persist rubric_hash with a relevance job; replay must pin the rubric.

findings.source_validator: live-UI cross-check during report screenshot capture; corrected re-capture + re-grade
findings.title: VALIDITY CORRECTION: original captures measured the wrong search engine for both stores; findings re-based
findings.summary: While capturing report screenshots, the live storefront contradicted the recorded data (e.g. IW "accent chair": Store API 0 vs storefront 6; SB "coffee table": loose query returned a false-positive ottoman that the real predictive search excludes). Root cause: (a) Industry West was captured via the WooCommerce Store API /wp-json/wc/store/v1/products?search=, but shoppers use the storefront /?s= engine (different, and for synonyms smarter); (b) Seven Bonde was captured via a loose products(query:) call, but its search box builds a strict AND-of-prefix Storefront GraphQL query (title:WORD* OR product_type:WORD* ...) AND-ed, first:8 — far narrower. Both engines were re-captured faithfully (paced, no server load) and re-graded under pinned rubric 99a0e992a992. NET CHANGE: story flipped from "IW precise/narrow vs SB broad/noisy" to IW=broad-but-fuzzy (23/58 answered, 14% not-relevant) vs SB=precise-but-narrow (15/58 answered, 5% not-relevant); both fail attributes and natural-language intent. Corrected numbers now drive the board and the report. Lesson captured in the furniture-search-eval skill (measure the real shopper engine). Evidence: assessments/industrywest/search-eval/SE-20260713/ (iw-sf-captures.json, iw-sf-ndcg.json, sb2-captures.json, sb2-ndcg.json, eval-board.json).

findings.title: General-retail pilot: Target search is wide but shallow on compositional intent, with a narrower substring-synonym gap (101-term eval)
findings.summary: [EXPANDED 2026-08-09 to 110 terms, rubric 99a0e992a992] Target on-site search, 110 terms x 5 datasets, 721 product judgments. Overall mean grade 1.73/3, 38% not-relevant. STRONG on product-type, attribute (1.73/3), brand, and most synonyms (synonym 1.91/3, literal 2.00/3). Brand-name queries (threshold, cat and jack, good and gather) REDIRECT to curated brand pages (2,710/1,776/1,649 results) - verified live and counted as answered, not 0-result failures. TWO gaps: (1) compositional natural-language intent is the clear weakness - job-function 1.33/3, 63% not-relevant: move-into-a-new-house -> romance novels & toy food trucks; set-up-a-home-theater -> pajamas + soundbars; intent works only when the phrase maps to a real category (healthy snacks for kids, home gym equipment, organize my kitchen). (2) Narrower regional/substring-synonym gap - the engine substring-matches instead of mapping the word: pop/popsicle -> Pop-Tarts, ice-lolly -> mints, jumper -> baby activity jumpers, nappies -> mixed. VERIFY-THE-WORST applied (brand zeros were API-routing false negatives). Captured paced in-session at a human rate; PerimeterX bot protection respected, never bypassed (capture paused and resumed on natural cooldown). Synonym rows now annotated with their canonical lead node (compared_to): UK/regional variants underperform their US canonical (trainers 0.88 vs sneakers 1.88; rubbish bin 1.0 vs trash can 2.0; nappies 1.17 vs diapers 2.0), while crockpot=slow cooker and rc car=remote control car are perfect. Supersedes the 36-term 2026-08-08 board.
